# Take in work items and show them in an inbox

## Intent

nightshift owns a project's work, and a person steers it. Every piece of
work, whether typed as text, imported from an issue or imported as a spec
package, becomes a work item with one state out of a fixed set, and
everything that happens to it is written to a thread the person can read.
Where nightshift cannot go on by itself it asks through a durable decision
with fixed options, which waits in an inbox until the person answers, and
it tells the person that they are needed.

## Goals

- **One path for every kind of work.** A spec package, an issue imported
  from a forge and a change request typed as free text each become a work
  item with a number, a kind, a state and one thread.
- **One state machine for every item.** An item is in one of eleven states,
  and it moves only along the transitions this package allows; the packages
  that plan, implement, land and publish drive it through one function.
- **The inbox shows two things.** `Unread` holds what finished or changed
  since the person last looked; `Action` holds every decision that waits
  for them. Both are read over the HTTP API and through the `nightshift`
  command.
- **The person is never waited on by a process.** A question for the person
  is a durable decision. It never takes an option by itself, it survives a
  restart, and its answer takes effect within 5 seconds.
- **The person is told when they are needed.** A configured command runs
  when a decision opens, when a reminder is due and when the hub has been
  unreachable for 15 minutes.
- **The person can end an item.** `nightshift item abandon` ends an item
  that has not landed.

## Non-goals

This package is the third of ten written from
`docs/prd/02-drive-work-items-through-the-hub.md`. What its neighbourhood
holds that is another package's:

- **`01_daemon_api_and_credentials`**: the daemon, the API server, the
  client's base, the event log and its stream, the hub client and its

- **`02_workspaces_and_policy`**: registering a workspace, its settings and

  workspace remove` as commands. This package adds the item counts to the
  first and the refusal and the removal of threads to the second.
- **`04_sessions_and_scheduling`**: sessions, the scheduler, the daily
  limit with its `Unread` entry, pausing and the `paused` marker, the
  `session_failed` and `session_limit` decisions, and ending an abandoned

- **`05_planning`**: starting the planning of an item a person created,

- **`06_implementation_and_review`**: the `blocked` and

- **`07_landing`**: the `approval`, `conflict` and `policy` decisions, and

- **`08_health_and_publishing`**: the `main_red` and `origin` decisions,

No decision kind is declared by this package: each kind, its options and
what an answer does belong to the package named above. This package is the

Also out, for every package of that PRD: intake from forge webhooks, a web
or desktop client, an MCP facade for the inbox, and routing a decision to

## Background

Package 01 gives this package a daemon with an authenticated API under
`/api/v1`, a client with a command table, a store with migrations, an
event log whose events the stream `GET /api/v1/events` serves, and a hub
client with a monitor that knows since when the hub is unreachable and
which token the hub stopped accepting. Package 02 gives it registered
workspaces and a way to get a workspace's repository from the hub.

Parley (`agent-fox-dev/parley`) is the hub. What this package uses of it,
as its `docs/api.md` states at commit `7eabfb9`:

- `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/issues/{number}` answers the issue thread
  `{issue, comments, comments_next_cursor, comments_error}` with the first
  page of at most 100 comments, oldest first. An issue is `{number, title,
  body, state, url, author {login}, labels, created_at, updated_at,
  closed_at, is_pr}`; `labels` holds the names. When the comments could
  not be read the answer is still `200`, with `comments_error`
  `{error_type, message}`.
- `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/issues/{number}/comments` lists comments
  `{id, body, author {login}, created_at, updated_at, url}` oldest first as
  `{"items", "next_cursor"}`, read on with `cursor`.
- Both need `forge:read`, which the worker token's `forge:write`
  satisfies. A forge failure is the hub's error envelope with a
  `forge_…` type (`404 forge_not_found`, `502 forge_unreachable`, …).

`afspec` (`github.com/agent-fox-dev/spec/afspec`) loads and validates a
spec package and tells which of its tasks are open.

The inbox follows the pattern of Pizza Bot
(`github.com/agent-fox-dev/pizza-bot`): two global views over threads,
`Unread` for finished work and `Action` for durable approval requests,
served to thin clients over HTTP and server-sent events.

## Requirements

Constraint: Linux and macOS; Windows is best effort. Constraint: the
`nightshift` client speaks only the daemon's HTTP API, so every command
below has a route.

### Work items and intake

A work item belongs to one workspace and has a number unique in nightshift,
a kind (`spec`, `defect`, `change_request`), a title, its source, a state
and one thread. Numbers start at 1, rise by one over all workspaces and
are never given twice. There are three ways to create one:

- `nightshift item new <slug> --text "<text>" [--kind defect|change_request]
  [--no-plan-approval]` creates an item from free text (default kind
  `change_request`). The text is 1 to 20,000 characters; outside that the
  command exits 2. The item's title is the first line of the text, cut to
  80 characters.
- `nightshift item import <slug> --issue <N> [--no-plan-approval]` reads the
  issue and its comments through the hub's forge routes. The kind is
  `defect` when the issue carries `af:defect` or a label named `bug`, else
  `change_request`. The title is the issue's. An issue already imported is
  refused with exit code 1, naming the existing item. An issue that cannot
  be read is refused with the hub's error.
- `nightshift item import <slug> --spec <NN>` takes an active spec package
  on the default branch. The title is the package's. It is refused with
  exit code 1 when the package does not load (with the validator's first
  finding), is not `active`, has no task `pending` or `in_progress`, or is
  already an item.

Each prints the new item's number and its thread's URL path:

```text
item 12
thread /api/v1/threads/31
```

An item is created in the state `new`. This package stores
`--no-plan-approval` with the item; package 05 starts the planning and acts
on it.

The routes behind the commands:

| Route | Body | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/items` | `{"workspace", "text", "kind"?, "no_plan_approval"?}` | `201` with the item |
| `POST /api/v1/items/import` | `{"workspace", "issue": N, "no_plan_approval"?}` or `{"workspace", "spec": "NN"}` | `201` with the item |
| `GET /api/v1/items` | `workspace=<slug>`, `state=<s>` | `200` `{"items": […]}`, by number |
| `GET /api/v1/items/{number}` | | `200` with the item |
| `POST /api/v1/items/{number}/abandon` | | `200` with the item |

An item in JSON:

```json
{"number": 12, "workspace": "demo", "kind": "defect",
 "title": "Greeting drops the name", "state": "new",
 "state_since": "2026-11-28T10:00:00Z", "created_at": "2026-11-28T10:00:00Z",
 "plan_approval": true,
 "source": {"type": "issue", "issue": 7, "url": "https://…"},
 "parent": null, "children": [],
 "thread": "/api/v1/threads/31",
 "waiting_on": null, "markers": []}
```

`source.type` is `text`, `issue`, `spec` or `item` (for an item created
from another, see below). `GET /api/v1/items/{number}` adds the source's
content: the `text`; the issue's `title`, `body`, `labels` and `comments`;
or the package's `spec_id`, `spec_name` and directory.

A work item is in one of these states:

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `new` | Created; no session has worked on it |
| `planning` | A plan is being drafted or reviewed |
| `awaiting_approval` | A `plan` decision in `Action` asks the person to approve the plan |
| `ready` | Approved, or an imported package; waits for a free session, the daily limit or a dependency |
| `implementing` | An implementer session works in the item's fork |
| `reviewing` | The reviewer works on the change's current version |
| `landing` | The gate and the review passed; the land is requested or waits on a person or on the workspace |
| `verifying` | Landed; the health command runs |
| `publishing` | Healthy; the push to origin is requested or waits on a person |
| `done` | Landed, the main branch healthy, and the commit on origin |
| `abandoned` | Ended without landing, by the person |

The packages that drive an item move it through one function, which allows
these transitions and refuses every other, a move to the state the item is
in among them:

| From | To |
|---|---|
| `new` | `planning`, `ready`, `abandoned` |
| `planning` | `awaiting_approval`, `ready`, `abandoned` |
| `awaiting_approval` | `planning`, `ready`, `abandoned` |
| `ready` | `implementing`, `abandoned` |
| `implementing` | `reviewing`, `abandoned` |
| `reviewing` | `implementing`, `landing`, `abandoned` |
| `landing` | `implementing`, `verifying`, `abandoned` |
| `verifying` | `publishing`, `awaiting_approval` |
| `publishing` | `done` |
| `done`, `abandoned` | none |

Every transition is written to the item's thread and to the event log.

An item that waits for a decision keeps its state and names the decision in
`waiting_on`: the id, the kind and the question of the item's oldest open
decision, or `null`. `nightshift item list [<slug>] [--state <s>]` lists
items, one line each: number, workspace, state, markers, what it waits on,
title. `nightshift item show <N>` prints one with what it waits for.

`nightshift item abandon <N>` ends the item's sessions, abandons its change
and sets `abandoned`; it is refused with exit code 1 for an item that is
`verifying`, `publishing` or `done`, and for one already `abandoned`. The
first two are hooks packages 04 and 05 register; this package calls them in
the order they were registered, closes the item's open decisions with the
reason `item abandoned`, and sets the state.

**An item made from another.** Packages 05 and 06 create items from an
item: the parts of work too large for one package, and the open items of an
implementation. This package offers the function: the new item is in the
state `new`, of the kind and with the text it is given, linked to the item
it came from (`parent`, and the parent's `children`), and the parent's
thread gets an entry naming it. Such an item is not planned until the
person asks (package 05).

**Workspaces.** `nightshift workspace list` (package 02) shows with each
workspace its counts of open work items: how many are in each state other
than `done` and `abandoned`. `nightshift workspace remove <slug>` is refused
with exit code 1 while the workspace has a work item that is neither `done`
nor `abandoned`, naming them (`workspace demo has open work items: 12
(ready), 14 (landing)`); otherwise the workspace's items and all of its
threads are removed from nightshift with it. The counts are the member
`items` of the workspace object (`{"ready": 2, "landing": 1}`), printed as
`3 open (2 ready, 1 landing)` or `0 open`.

### The inbox

Every work item has one thread; a workspace has one more for what concerns
no single item (the workspace turning `red` or `held` with no item to
blame, the daily limit, the hub's outage); the installation has one for the
daily brief. A thread is a list of entries in the order they happened, each
with a time, a kind and a text: the item's state changes, each session's
start and end with its role and tokens, each check reported, each land
attempt, each push to origin, and each decision with its answer. nightshift
writes the entries from what it did and what the hub reported; no agent
writes to a thread directly. The entries of this package are the item's
creation, its state changes, an item made from it, a decision opened,
answered or closed, a reminder, the hub's outage and a token the hub
stopped accepting; the other packages write theirs through the same
function.

A thread is **unread** from an entry of a kind that marks it (the item
`done` or `abandoned`, a decision opened, a revert, a repair, the daily
limit, the hub's outage, a brief) until the person opens it (`GET` of the
thread through the client, or `nightshift thread show <id>`) or marks it
read. The writer of an entry says whether it marks the thread.

A **decision** has an id, a kind, the item and thread, a question in one
sentence, its evidence (links to the change, the version's diff, the
sessions' streams and the texts named for its kind), its options with one
marked as recommended and one line on what each does, what it blocks, and,
once answered, the option, the comment and the time. The kinds and their
options are the ones the source PRD names: `plan`, `session_failed`,
`session_limit`, `review_disagreement`, `approval`, `blocked`, `conflict`,
`main_red`, `origin`, `policy` and `rule`. Each is declared, in a registry
this package keeps, by the package that owns it: its name, its options with
the line on what each does and whether it requires a comment. Another
package can add an option to a declared kind, and registers for a kind and
an option the handler that carries out an answer.

A decision waits until it is answered; it never takes an option by
itself. One that has been open for 24 hours puts one reminder entry in its
thread, marking it unread, and again every 24 hours.

A decision can be closed without an answer by the package that opened it,
with a reason (`superseded by a note`, `item abandoned`); a closed decision
is no longer in `Action` and cannot be answered.

**Telling the person.** When `[notify].command` is configured, nightshift
runs that command, as the daemon's user, each time a decision opens, a
reminder is due, a workspace turns `red` or `held`, the hub has been
unreachable for 15 minutes, or a brief is written. The command gets one
JSON document on its standard input: `event` (`decision_opened`,
`decision_reminder`, `workspace_red`, `workspace_held`, `hub_unreachable`
or `brief`), `time`, the `workspace` and `item` where there are any, the
thread's URL path, and for a decision its `id`, `kind`, `question` and
option keys:

```json
{"event": "decision_opened", "time": "2026-11-28T10:00:00Z",
 "workspace": "demo", "item": 12, "thread": "/api/v1/threads/31",
 "decision": {"id": 5, "kind": "plan",
              "question": "Approve the plan for item 12?",
              "options": ["approve", "revise", "abandon"]}}
```

A command that exits other than 0, or runs longer than 30 seconds and is
ended, is noted in the daemon's log with its exit code and the first line
of its error output; it is not run again for that event, and nothing waits
for it. Without the key, nothing is run.

**The hub's outage.** After 15 minutes without the hub, one entry goes to
`Unread` saying so (`hub unreachable since <time>`), in the thread of every
registered workspace, and the notification `hub_unreachable` is sent once;
it is not repeated until the hub has been reachable in between. A token
that the hub stops accepting while the daemon runs is named in one `Unread`
entry (`worker token: 401 unauthenticated`), written the same way and not
repeated until the hub accepted the token in between.

The API serves `GET /api/v1/threads` (with `view=all|unread|action`, a
workspace filter, newest activity first, 50 per page), `GET
/api/v1/threads/:id`, `POST /api/v1/threads/:id/read`, `GET
/api/v1/decisions` (open ones unless `state=all`), `GET
/api/v1/decisions/:id` and `POST /api/v1/decisions/:id/answer` with
`{"option", "comment"?, "record"?}`. An answer naming an option the
decision does not have is `400` with `error_type: unknown_option`; a
missing required comment is `400` with `error_type: comment_required`; a
second answer to an answered decision is `409` with `error_type:
already_answered` and the first answer in the body. An answer takes effect
within 5 seconds: the item's next step is started or queued, and the thread
shows it.

A list answers `{"items": […], "next_cursor": <string or null>}` and is
read on with `cursor`. A thread in a list:

```json
{"id": 31, "path": "/api/v1/threads/31", "kind": "item",
 "workspace": "demo", "item": 12, "title": "Greeting drops the name",
 "unread": true, "last_activity": "2026-11-28T10:05:00Z",
 "open_decisions": [{"id": 5, "kind": "plan", "question": "…"}]}
```

`kind` is `item`, `workspace` or `brief`. `GET /api/v1/threads/:id` adds
`entries`, each `{"seq", "time", "kind", "text", "unread"}`, and
`decisions`, every decision of the thread. A decision:

```json
{"id": 5, "kind": "plan", "state": "open", "thread": "/api/v1/threads/31",
 "workspace": "demo", "item": 12,
 "question": "Approve the plan for item 12?",
 "evidence": [{"label": "draft change", "url": "https://…"},
              {"label": "reviewer's verdict", "text": "agree"}],
 "options": [{"key": "approve", "does": "activates the package",
              "comment_required": false, "recommended": true}],
 "blocks": "item 12", "opened_at": "2026-11-28T10:00:00Z",
 "answer": null, "closed_reason": null}
```

`state` is `open`, `answered` or `closed`; an answer is `{"option",
"comment", "record", "time"}`.

The client mirrors these: `nightshift inbox [--unread|--action]` (the
default shows `Action` first, then `Unread`), `nightshift thread show <id>`,
`nightshift decision show <id>`, `nightshift decide <id> --option <key>
[--comment "<text>"] [--record]`, and `nightshift watch`, which prints one
line per event from the stream until interrupted. Every command prints text
for a terminal and, with `--json`, the API's JSON. Exit codes: 0 on
success, 1 when the daemon refuses or cannot be reached (`cannot reach
nightshiftd at <address>`), 2 for a usage error.

**It survives a restart.** After `nightshiftd` stops, by signal or by
crash, no item, thread, entry or decision is lost, an answer whose effect
was not yet carried out is carried out at the next start, and a reminder
that fell due meanwhile is written once.

### End-to-end flows

**A text becomes an item, and a decision about it is answered.** The person
runs `nightshift item new demo --text "Add a greeting endpoint"` and reads
the item's number and its thread's path. A later package opens a decision
for the item; the configured command receives `decision_opened`; the
decision is in `nightshift inbox --action`. The person runs `nightshift
decide <id> --option approve`. Within 5 seconds the handler registered for
that option has run, and `nightshift thread show <id>` shows the item's
creation, the decision, its answer and what the handler did.

**An issue is imported, abandoned, and its workspace removed.** The person
runs `nightshift item import demo --issue 7`. `nightshiftd` reads the issue
and its comments from the hub; the issue carries `bug`, so the item is a
`defect`. A second import of the issue is refused, naming the item.
`nightshift workspace remove demo` is refused, naming the item. The person
runs `nightshift item abandon <N>`; the thread is in `Unread`. `nightshift
workspace remove demo` now succeeds, and the item and its thread are gone.

**The hub is away for 15 minutes.** The hub stops answering. After 15
minutes the thread of workspace `demo` is in `Unread` with `hub unreachable
since <time>` and the configured command receives `hub_unreachable`.
Another 15 minutes add nothing. The hub answers again, then goes away
again; 15 minutes later the entry and the notification come a second time.

## Design Decisions

From the source PRD, by its numbers:

- **3. The plan's approval is the one go-ahead; an imported spec package
  needs none.** The owner decided it. Here: an imported package becomes an
  item in `new`, and the transition `new` to `ready` exists for it.
- **21. An unanswered decision waits; API and command-line client in
  version 1; one daemon and one person.** Kept from PRD 01, where the owner
  decided it.
- **30. Open items a session reports become unplanned `defect` items.**
  Kept from PRD 01. Here: the function that creates an item from another.
- **31. 24-hour reminders** are a starting value.
- **35. The parts of work too large for one package become new, unplanned
  items.** The owner decided it. Here: the same function.
- **37, 42. Telling the person is one command, not a list of
  integrations.** The owner decided it on the comparison of decision 37;
  the form is chosen there.

Chosen here:

1. **This package is the third of ten.** The owner agreed to the split on
   2026-11-28; this package holds *Work items and intake* and *The inbox*.
2. **Three Go packages: `internal/inbox` (threads, entries, decisions,
   reminders), `internal/item` (work items, which imports `inbox`) and
   `internal/notify`.** Why: an item needs its thread, a thread needs no
   item, and the notification command is called by packages 07, 08 and 10
   as well.
3. **`waiting_on` is read from the inbox, not stored: the item's oldest
   open decision.** Why: one fact kept in two places goes out of step, and
   an item with two open decisions still names one.
4. **The transitions are the table in *Work items and intake*, by state
   alone and not by kind; a move to the current state is refused.** Why: it
   is every move the source PRD describes (`verifying` to
   `awaiting_approval` is the revert, `landing` to `implementing` a
   conflict, a rejection or a note), and a later package that needs another
   has found a gap in the PRD, not in the table.
5. **Item routes: `POST /api/v1/items`, `POST /api/v1/items/import`, `GET
   /api/v1/items`, `GET /api/v1/items/{number}`, `POST
   /api/v1/items/{number}/abandon`.** Why: the source PRD names the
   commands and no routes for them.
6. **A text outside 1 to 20,000 characters is refused by the client with
   exit code 2 and by the API with `400 invalid_request`; characters are
   Unicode code points.** Why: the API has other clients later.
7. **The title of a text item is the first line of the text, cut to 80
   characters.** Why: the source PRD gives an item a title and the command
   no way to state one.
8. **Labels are compared ignoring case.** Why: forges treat `Bug` and `bug`
   as one label.
9. **An issue is refused when its comments cannot be read
   (`comments_error`), and when its number is a pull request's (`is_pr`).**
   Why: the source PRD has the item carry "the issue and its comments", and
   a pull request is not an issue.
10. **At most 1,000 comments of an issue are read; an issue with more is
    imported with the first 1,000 and `source.comments_truncated: true`.**
    Why: the loop over the comment pages needs a bound.
11. **A refused import: `404 not_found` for a package number that names no
    package, `409 conflict` for the other refusals of a package and for
    something already imported, `502 hub_error` carrying the hub's
    `error_type` and message for a hub error, `503 hub_unavailable` while
    the hub is unreachable or the worker token is not accepted.** Why: the
    source PRD gives the exit code 1 and no status.
12. **"Already imported" counts every item of the workspace, an abandoned
    one included.** Why: the source PRD makes no exception.
13. **A spec package is looked up in `.specs/` of the default branch's
    tip: the workspace object's `head_sha`, brought into a clone of its own
    (`<clones_dir>/<slug>.import`) with `gitclone.Sync`.** Why: `.specs/`
    is the spec root's default and the source PRD names no other; the
    clone package 02 keeps per workspace is the health command's.
14. **`--no-plan-approval` with `--spec`, `--issue` together with `--spec`
    or neither, and `--kind spec` are usage errors.** Why: the source PRD
    gives the option only to the two commands whose items are planned.
15. **A hook that fails does not stop an abandon: the failure is written
    to the thread and the item is `abandoned` all the same.** Why: the
    person asked to stop; the hook's owner tries its own hub call again.
16. **Abandoning an item closes its open decisions with the reason `item
    abandoned`; abandoning an abandoned item is refused.** Why: a decision
    about an ended item must not stay in `Action`.
17. **A decision has the states `open`, `answered` and `closed`; an answer
    to a closed one is `409 conflict`.** Why: the source PRD closes a `plan`
    decision as `superseded by a note`.
18. **A kind declares its options; the recommended one is named when a
    decision is opened; a decision keeps the options it was opened with.**
    Why: which option to recommend depends on the case, and a decision must
    read the same after a restart or a later registration.
19. **An answer is stored first and carried out by the option's handler
    afterwards: at once, at the next start when the daemon stopped in
    between, and again every 30 seconds while the handler returns an error,
    the first error written to the thread. A handler may be called twice
    for one answer.** Why: the answer must not be lost, and the usual
    error, the hub being away, ends by itself.
20. **The writer of an entry says whether it marks the thread unread;
    entry kinds are free names.** Why: the kinds that mark belong to seven
    packages.
21. **`GET /api/v1/threads/:id` marks the thread read and answers `unread`
    as it was before.** Why: the source PRD counts a `GET` through the
    client as opening it, and the client still shows what was new.
22. **A reminder is due 24 hours after the later of the opening and the
    last reminder; a daemon that was stopped for several days writes one.**
    Why: three reminders at once say nothing more than one.
23. **The entries for the hub's outage and for a token go to the thread of
    every registered workspace; the notification `hub_unreachable` is sent
    once, without a workspace or a thread; with no workspace nothing is
    written.** Why: the source PRD puts the hub's outage in the workspace's
    thread, and the installation's thread is for the brief.
24. **The notification command is run with `sh -c` by `internal/notify`
    itself, not through `internal/command`.** Why: package 04 makes that
    package run as the session user, and this command runs as the daemon's.
25. **A decision in the notification's JSON is the member `decision`
    (`id`, `kind`, `question`, `options`).** Why: the source PRD lists the
    members and not their nesting.
26. **Notification commands still running at shutdown are ended.** Why:
    nothing waits for them.
27. **Removing a workspace removes its items with its threads, entries
    and decisions; item numbers are not given again.** Why: an item has one
    thread, and the removal is refused unless every item is finished.
28. **`nightshift watch` reconnects with its last `seq` when the stream
    ends, and exits 1 when it cannot connect or the cursor expired.** Why:
    the daemon disconnects a client that fell behind (package 01).
29. **An item carries `markers`, names that functions other packages
    register report for it (`paused`, `taken over`).** Why: `item list` and
    `item show` print them, and they are packages 04's and 09's.
30. **Event types: `item.created`, `item.updated`, `thread.updated`,
    `thread.removed`, `decision.opened`, `decision.answered`,
    `decision.closed`.**

## Glossary

- **work item**: one piece of work nightshift drives to a published
  change: a spec package, a defect or a change request.
- **intake**: creating a work item, from text, from an issue or from a
  spec package.
- **thread**: the record of one work item (or of a workspace, or of the
  briefs) as the inbox shows it, written by nightshift from what happened.
- **entry**: one line of a thread, with a time, a kind and a text.
- **decision**: a question to the person with fixed options, kept in the
  inbox until answered or closed.
- **decision kind**: the name under which a package declares the options
  of its decisions and what each does.
- **handler**: the function a package registers for a kind and an option,
  which carries out an answer.
- **Unread**: the view of threads with something new since the person last
  opened them.
- **Action**: the view of threads with an open decision.
- **`waiting_on`**: the open decision an item waits for.
- **marker**: a name another package reports for an item, `paused` or
  `taken over`.
- **hub**: a Parley server (`parleyd`).
- **package, `active`, task**: as the spec format of `agent-fox-dev/spec`
  defines them.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Intake: three ways to create a work item

**Rationale:** Work reaches nightshift as a text, an issue or a finished spec package, and each has to become the same thing before one process can drive it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN an authenticated client sends `POST /api/v1/items` with `{"workspace", "text", "kind"?, "no_plan_approval"?}`, the workspace is registered, the text has 1 to 20,000 Unicode code points and `kind` is absent, `defect` or `change_request`, THE nightshiftd SHALL store a work item with the next number (one above the highest number ever given over all workspaces, starting at 1), the kind (`change_request` when absent), the title (the first line of the text, cut to 80 code points), the source `{type: "text"}` with the text, the state `new` and `plan_approval` (false when `no_plan_approval` is true, else true); create the item's thread with a first entry of kind `created`; append the event `item.created`; and call every creation hook registered with `OnCreated`
   → status 201 with the item as {number, workspace, kind, title, state, state_since, created_at, plan_approval, source {type, …}, parent, children, thread, waiting_on, markers}, `thread` being `/api/v1/threads/<id>`; items created by concurrent requests get distinct numbers with no gap; the event's data is `{item, workspace, state, thread}`
   Check: integration
   - setup: an inbox and an item service over a copy of the store template and the event log; the workspaces `demo` and `other` are known through the service's workspace source (the Get and List of package 02's workspace.Service), a stub in the tests of this package that need no removal
   - setup: one creation hook registered that records its argument
   ```
   new file internal/item/routes_test.go, through the router, a table over {text only -> kind change_request, plan_approval true; kind defect; no_plan_approval true -> plan_approval false; a text of 3 lines -> title is line 1; a first line of 200 code points -> title has 80; a text of exactly 20,000 code points -> 201}: r = post('/api/v1/items', body); assert r.status == 201; assert r.json fields; assert get('/api/v1/threads/' + id).json.entries[0].kind == 'created'; assert the event log's last event type == 'item.created'; assert the creation hook saw the item. Then 20 concurrent posts over two workspaces: assert the numbers are 1 more than before .. 20 more, each once
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF a request to `POST /api/v1/items` has a body that is not a JSON object, names no workspace, carries a text that is empty or longer than 20,000 Unicode code points or a `kind` other than `defect` and `change_request`, or names a workspace that is not registered, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL refuse the request and store nothing
   → status 400 with `error_type: invalid_request` and a message naming the member, or status 404 with `error_type: not_found` for the unregistered workspace; no item, no thread and no event is written, and the next item created gets the number it would have got
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/item/routes_test.go, a table over {'not json', {} , text '', text of 20,001 code points, a text of 20,000 two-byte characters -> 201 (counted in code points, not bytes), kind 'spec', kind 'bogus' -> 400 invalid_request; workspace 'nope' -> 404 not_found}: r = post('/api/v1/items', body); assert r.status and r.json.error_type; assert count(items) and count(threads) unchanged; then a valid post gets number previous+1
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] WHEN an authenticated client sends `POST /api/v1/items/import` with `{"workspace", "issue": N, "no_plan_approval"?}` for a registered workspace, and the hub answers `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/issues/{N}` with an issue that is not a pull request and whose comments it could read, THE nightshiftd SHALL read the issue with the worker token, read the further comments from `GET …/issues/{N}/comments` with `cursor` set to each `next_cursor` until it is null or 1,000 comments are read, and store a work item in the state `new` whose kind is `defect` when the issue's labels hold `af:defect` or `bug`, compared ignoring case, and `change_request` otherwise, whose title is the issue's title and whose source is `{type: "issue", issue, url, title, body, labels, comments: [{author, body, created_at}], comments_truncated}`; then create the thread, append the event and call the creation hooks as for a text
   → status 201 with the item; `GET /api/v1/items/{number}` answers the source with every comment read, oldest first; `comments_truncated` is true only when the hub had more than 1,000 comments; the hub saw requests bearing the worker token only
   Check: integration
   - setup: internal/hubtest extended with scriptable issues: an issue thread per workspace and number, its comments paged 100 a page, a `comments_error`, `is_pr` and a forge error to answer with
   - setup: the item service's hub client pointed at the fake hub
   ```
   new file internal/item/import_test.go, through the router, a table over the fake hub's issue 7 {labels ['bug'] -> defect; ['af:defect'] -> defect; ['Bug','ui'] -> defect; ['ui'] -> change_request; [] -> change_request; 250 comments over 3 pages -> source.comments has 250 in order; 1,100 comments -> 1,000 and comments_truncated true; no_plan_approval true -> plan_approval false}: r = post('/api/v1/items/import', {workspace: 'demo', issue: 7}); assert r.status == 201; assert kind, title, source; assert every hub request bore the worker token
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF an issue import names an issue that an item of the workspace was already created from, or the hub is not available to the worker token, or the hub answers the issue or a page of its comments with an error, or the issue's answer carries a `comments_error`, or the issue has `is_pr: true`, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL refuse the import and store nothing, checking for the existing item before any request to the hub
   → status 409 `conflict` with the message `issue #<N> is already item <M>` (also when item M is `abandoned`), sending no hub request; status 503 `hub_unavailable` while `Available(worker)` is false; status 502 `hub_error` with the message `<hub error_type>: <hub message>` for a hub error and for a `comments_error`; status 409 `conflict` with `#<N> is a pull request`; status 400 `invalid_request` for an `issue` that is not a positive integer or a body carrying both `issue` and `spec` or neither; status 404 `not_found` for a workspace that is not registered; in every case no item, thread or event is written
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/item/import_test.go, a table over {issue 7 imported before -> 409 'issue #7 is already item 1' and hub request count unchanged; the same after item 1 was abandoned -> 409; fake hub stopped and the monitor unreachable -> 503 hub_unavailable; issue answers 404 forge_not_found -> 502 'forge_not_found: the forge answered 404: 404 Not Found'; comments page 2 answers 502 forge_unreachable -> 502 hub_error; comments_error {forge_timeout} -> 502 hub_error 'forge_timeout: …'; is_pr true -> 409 '#7 is a pull request'; issue 0, issue 'x', both issue and spec, neither -> 400; workspace 'nope' -> 404}: assert r.status, r.json.error_type, r.json.message; assert count(items) unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] WHEN an authenticated client sends `POST /api/v1/items/import` with `{"workspace", "spec": "NN"}` for a registered workspace, and the package with that number in `.specs/` at the tip of the workspace's default branch loads, validates with no error, has the status `active` and has at least one open task, THE nightshiftd SHALL read the workspace's `head_sha` from the hub, bring a clone of the workspace to that commit with `gitclone.Sync` of package 02, find the package directory with `afspec.DiscoverSpecs`, load it with `afspec.LoadSpec`, validate it with `afspec.ValidateInRoot` and read its open tasks with `OpenTasks`, and store a work item in the state `new` with the kind `spec`, the package's title, `plan_approval` true and the source `{type: "spec", spec_id, spec_name, dir}`; then create the thread, append the event and call the creation hooks as for a text
   → status 201 with the item; `source.dir` is the package's directory relative to the repository root (`.specs/04_greeting`); the item's state is `new`
   Check: integration
   - setup: the function that yields a checkout of the default branch's tip is a parameter of the item service; production passes the one built on the hub client's Workspace and gitclone.Sync
   - setup: internal/hubtest's workspace object carries `head_sha`, the head of its repository fixture
   ```
   in internal/item/import_test.go: root = a temporary repository tree whose .specs holds package 04, built with afspec (CreateSpec, filled, saved, moved to active through Spec.Transition, its task 1 pending); the item service is given a checkout function returning that tree in place of the gitclone call; r = post('/api/v1/items/import', {workspace: 'demo', spec: '04'}); assert r.status == 201; assert r.json.kind == 'spec'; assert r.json.title == the package's title; assert r.json.source == {type: 'spec', spec_id: '04', spec_name: 'greeting', dir: '.specs/04_greeting'}; assert r.json.state == 'new'. One case with the production checkout function against the fake hub's git endpoint and repository fixture (package 02), the fixture's head commit holding package 04: assert 201 and that the clone directory is <clones_dir>/demo.import at the fixture's head
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] IF a spec import names a number no package on the default branch has, or a package that does not load or has a validation error, is not `active`, has no task `pending` or `in_progress`, or that an item of the workspace was already created from, or the default branch cannot be fetched, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL refuse the import and store nothing
   → status 404 `not_found` with `package <NN> not found on the default branch`; status 409 `conflict` with `package <NN> does not load: <the load error, or the first validation error as <check>: <message>>`, `package <NN> is <status>, not active`, `package <NN> has no open task` or `package <NN> is already item <M>`; status 503 `hub_unavailable` while `Available(worker)` is false and 502 `hub_error` with the fetch's error; status 400 `invalid_request` for a `spec` that is not a string of two or more digits or a body with `no_plan_approval` beside `spec`; no item, thread or event is written
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/item/import_test.go, a table over fixture trees {no package 09 -> 404; package 05 with requirements.json cut off -> 409 starting 'package 05 does not load: '; package 06 whose task names an unknown criterion -> 409 'package 06 does not load: C4: …' (the first entry of ValidateInRoot's Errors); package 07 in draft -> 409 'package 07 is draft, not active'; package 08 with every task done -> 409 'package 08 has no open task'; package 04 imported before -> 409 'package 04 is already item 1'; checkout function failing -> 502 hub_error; monitor unreachable -> 503; spec '4', spec 4 (a number), spec with no_plan_approval -> 400}: assert r.status, r.json.error_type and r.json.message; assert count(items) unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-1.7] WHEN the person runs `nightshift item new <slug> --text "<text>" [--kind defect|change_request] [--no-plan-approval]`, `nightshift item import <slug> --issue <N> [--no-plan-approval]` or `nightshift item import <slug> --spec <NN>`, the flags before or after the slug, THE nightshift SHALL send `POST /api/v1/items` or `POST /api/v1/items/import` with the slug as `workspace` and the flags as the body's members, and print the new item's number and its thread's URL path
   → exit code 0; stdout is the two lines `item <number>` and `thread <path>`; with `--json` stdout is the item as the API answered it; a refusal by the daemon is exit code 1 with the error's message on stderr

1. [REQ-1.8] IF a command of this package is given a command line it cannot send: `item new` without a slug or without `--text`, with a text that is empty or longer than 20,000 Unicode code points, or with a `--kind` other than `defect` and `change_request`; `item import` with both `--issue` and `--spec` or neither, with an `--issue` that is not a positive integer, a `--spec` that is not two or more digits, or `--no-plan-approval` beside `--spec`, THEN THE nightshift SHALL print the usage of the command and send no request
   → exit code 2; the usage on stderr; stdout is empty; the daemon received no request
   Check: unit

   ```
   new file internal/cli/usage_test.go, one table for every usage error of the commands this package adds; these rows: {['item','new'], ['item','new','demo'], ['item','new','demo','--text',''], ['item','new','demo','--text', 20,001 code points], ['item','new','demo','--text','t','--kind','spec'], ['item','import','demo'], ['item','import','demo','--issue','7','--spec','04'], ['item','import','demo','--issue','0'], ['item','import','demo','--spec','4'], ['item','import','demo','--spec','04','--no-plan-approval']}: code, stdout, stderr = cli.Run(args); assert code == 2; assert stderr contains 'usage: nightshift item'; assert stdout == ''; assert the httptest server saw no request
   ```

### REQ-2: Item states, queries, abandoning and linked items

**Rationale:** Seven later packages move items; one function that knows every allowed move keeps an item from reaching a state by a road the person was never shown.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a part of nightshift calls the item service's `Transition(ctx, number, to, reason)` with a state the transition table allows from the item's current state (new -> planning, ready, abandoned; planning -> awaiting_approval, ready, abandoned; awaiting_approval -> planning, ready, abandoned; ready -> implementing, abandoned; implementing -> reviewing, abandoned; reviewing -> implementing, landing, abandoned; landing -> implementing, verifying, abandoned; verifying -> publishing, awaiting_approval; publishing -> done; done and abandoned -> none), THE nightshiftd SHALL set the item's state and `state_since`, append to the item's thread an entry of kind `state` with the text `<from> -> <to>`, followed by `: <reason>` when a reason is given, marking the thread unread when the new state is `done` or `abandoned`, append the event `item.updated` with the data `{item, workspace, state, thread}`, and then call every hook registered with `OnChange` with the item before and after
   → the call returns the item in its new state; the state, the entry and the event are written in one store transaction; a hook's error is written to the daemon's log and undoes nothing
   Check: unit
   - setup: an item service over a copy of the store template with an injected clock
   - setup: a test helper that puts an item into any state by walking allowed transitions
   ```
   new file internal/item/item_test.go, a table with one row per allowed pair of the transition table (22 rows), each on an item put into the from state: it = svc.Transition(ctx, n, to, 'because'); assert it.State == to; assert the thread's last entry == {kind: 'state', text: from + ' -> ' + to + ': because'}; assert thread.unread == (to in {done, abandoned}); assert the event log's last event == item.updated with state to; assert the OnChange hook saw (from, to). One row with an empty reason asserts the text has no colon suffix; one hook returning an error leaves the state at to
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF `Transition` is called for a number no item has, with a name that is not one of the eleven states, with the state the item is in, or with a state the transition table does not allow from the item's current state, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL refuse the transition and leave the item as it is
   → the call returns `item.ErrNotFound` for the unknown number and otherwise an error that is `item.ErrTransition` and whose text is `item <N>: <from> -> <to> is not allowed`; no state, entry or event is written and no hook is called; of two concurrent calls for the same allowed move exactly one succeeds and the other gets `ErrTransition`
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/item/item_test.go, a table over every ordered pair of the eleven states that the transition table does not hold (99 rows, the 11 same-state pairs among them) plus {unknown number -> ErrNotFound, to 'bogus' -> ErrTransition}: err = svc.Transition(ctx, n, to, ''); assert errors.Is(err, want); assert state, entry count and event count unchanged. Then 8 goroutines call Transition(n, 'planning') on one new item: assert exactly 1 nil error and 7 ErrTransition, and one `state` entry
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] WHEN an authenticated client requests `GET /api/v1/items`, optionally with `workspace=<slug>` and `state=<state>`, THE nightshiftd SHALL answer every item, or those of the workspace and in the state named, in ascending order of number, each with `waiting_on` as `{id, kind, question}` of the item's oldest open decision or null, and `markers` as the names of the registered marker functions (`RegisterMarker(name, fn)`) that report true for the item, in registration order
   → status 200 with `{"items": [<item>, …]}`; an item is {number, workspace, kind, title, state, state_since, created_at, plan_approval, source {type, …}, parent, children, thread, waiting_on, markers} with `source` reduced to `{type}` and, by type, `issue` and `url`, or `spec_id` and `spec_name`, or `item`; no item matching is `{"items": []}`
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/item/routes_test.go: 5 items over two workspaces in the states new, new, ready, done, abandoned; item 2 has two open decisions (ids 3 and 5) of a test kind and one answered; a marker 'paused' registered that is true for item 3; a table over {no filter -> numbers [1,2,3,4,5]; workspace=demo -> its items; state=new -> [1,2]; workspace=demo&state=done -> [4]; state=reviewing -> []}: r = get('/api/v1/items' + query); assert numbers; assert item 2 waiting_on.id == 3; assert item 1 waiting_on == null; assert item 3 markers == ['paused']; assert no item carries source.text
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] WHEN an authenticated client requests `GET /api/v1/items/{number}` for an existing item, THE nightshiftd SHALL answer the item as the list does, with the whole of its source (the `text`; or the issue's `issue`, `url`, `title`, `body`, `labels`, `comments` and `comments_truncated`; or the package's `spec_id`, `spec_name` and `dir`; or the `item` it was created from and the `text`), its `parent` and its `children` in ascending order
   → status 200 with the item; `waiting_on` and `markers` as in the list
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/item/routes_test.go, a table over {a text item -> source.text is the posted text; an item with an open decision -> waiting_on == {id, kind, question}; a parent with two linked items -> children == [n1, n2]; a linked item -> parent == p and source == {type: 'item', item: p, text}}: r = get('/api/v1/items/' + n); assert r.status == 200; assert the members
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] IF a request to `GET /api/v1/items`, `GET /api/v1/items/{number}` or `POST /api/v1/items/{number}/abandon` names a number no item has, a number that is not a positive decimal integer, a `state` that is not one of the eleven states, or a `workspace` that is not registered, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL refuse the request and change nothing
   → status 404 `not_found` for the unknown number and the unregistered workspace; status 400 `invalid_request` for the malformed number and the unknown state; the body is `{"error_type", "message"}`
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/item/routes_test.go, a table over {GET /api/v1/items/999 -> 404; GET /api/v1/items/abc, /api/v1/items/0, /api/v1/items/-1 -> 400; POST /api/v1/items/999/abandon -> 404; GET /api/v1/items?state=bogus -> 400; GET /api/v1/items?workspace=nope -> 404}: assert r.status and r.json.error_type
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] WHEN an authenticated client sends `POST /api/v1/items/{number}/abandon`, or a part of nightshift calls the item service's `Abandon(ctx, number, reason)`, for an item in the state `new`, `planning`, `awaiting_approval`, `ready`, `implementing`, `reviewing` or `landing`, THE nightshiftd SHALL call every hook registered with `OnAbandon(name, fn)` with the item, in registration order, writing a hook's error to the item's thread as an entry of kind `abandon_hook_failed` with the text `<name>: <error>` and going on; close every open decision of the item with the reason `item abandoned`; and move the item to `abandoned` through the transition function
   → status 200 with the item, its state `abandoned` and `waiting_on` null (the function returns the same item); the item's thread is unread; every hook was called once, before the state changed; the item's former open decisions have the state `closed`

### REQ-3: Threads, unread, and a workspace's removal

**Rationale:** The person reads what happened in one place per item, and should be shown only what is new since they last looked.

   → a thread has an id (a positive integer, never given twice), a kind, the workspace and the item where it has them, and a title: the item's title, `workspace <slug>` or `daily brief`; concurrent first calls of `WorkspaceThread` for one slug return the same id

### REQ-4: Decisions: a registry of kinds, answers and their handlers

**Rationale:** Eleven kinds of question from seven packages reach the person through one machinery, so that every one of them waits, is answered and takes effect in the same way.

#### Criteria

[REQ-4.1] WHEN a part of nightshift calls the inbox's `Open(ctx, OpenRequest{Kind, Thread, Question, Evidence, Recommended, Blocks})` with a kind declared through `RegisterKind(Kind{Name, Options: [{Key, Does, CommentRequired}]})`, an existing thread, a question that is not empty and a `Recommended` that is the key of one of the kind's options, THE nightshiftd SHALL store a decision in the state `open` with the next id (starting at 1), the thread and its workspace and item, the question, the evidence, what it blocks and a copy of the kind's options as they are at that moment, the options added through `AddOption(kind, Option)` among them and the recommended one marked; append to the thread an entry of kind `decision_opened` with the text `<kind>: <question>`, marking it unread; and append the event `decision.opened` with the data `{decision, kind, thread, workspace, item}`
   → the call returns the decision as {id, kind, state, thread, workspace, item, question, evidence: [{label, url or text}], options: [{key, does, comment_required, recommended}], blocks, opened_at, answer, closed_reason} with `answer` and `closed_reason` null; exactly one option has `recommended: true`; an option added to the kind after the decision was opened does not appear in it; the thread is in the views `unread` and `action`
   Check: unit
   - setup: an inbox over a copy of the store template with an injected clock, and an item thread t for item 12

### REQ-5: Waiting, reminding and telling the person

**Rationale:** A decision that waits in silence waits for days; the person has to learn that they are needed without watching the inbox, and nothing may be lost while they are away.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHILE a decision is open, THE nightshiftd SHALL take no option for it, however long it is open, and append to its thread an entry of kind `decision_reminder` with the text `<kind>: open since <opened_at>: <question>`, marking the thread unread, each time 24 hours have passed since the later of its opening and its last reminder, one entry also when several such periods have passed at once
   → a decision open for 23 hours 59 minutes has no reminder; one open for 24 hours has one; after 48 hours it has two; a daemon whose clock moved 7 days between two passes writes one reminder at that pass and the next one 24 hours later; the decision is still `open` with `answer` null; an answered or closed decision gets none
   Check: unit
   - setup: an inbox over a copy of the store template with an injected clock; the reminder period and the pass interval are parameters
   ```
   new file internal/inbox/reminder_test.go: decisions A (open), B (answered), C (closed) opened at T0; clock = T0+23h59m, inbox.RemindDue(ctx): assert no decision_reminder entry; clock = T0+24h, RemindDue: assert A's thread has 1 and is unread, B's and C's none; RemindDue again at the same time: still 1; clock = T0+48h: 2; clock = T0+48h+7d, RemindDue: 3; clock += 23h: 3; clock += 1h: 4; assert A.State == 'open' and A.Answer == nil; assert the default period is 24 hours and the pass runs once a minute from a goroutine that stops with the daemon
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] WHERE `[notify].command` is configured, THE nightshiftd SHALL run that command with `sh -c` as the daemon's user each time a decision opens (`decision_opened`), a reminder entry is written (`decision_reminder`), the hub's outage is noted (`hub_unreachable`) or another package calls `Notify` of `internal/notify` with its event (`workspace_red`, `workspace_held`, `brief`), writing one JSON document to its standard input and closing it, and return to the caller without waiting for the command
   → the document has `event` and `time` (RFC 3339 UTC) and, where there are any, `workspace`, `item` and `thread` (the thread's URL path), absent otherwise; for the two decision events it has `decision: {id, kind, question, options: [<key>, …]}`; the command is started once per event; `Notify` returns before the command ends; without the key no process is started, and an unknown key under `[notify]` fails the `config` check
   Check: integration
   - setup: the notifier is an interface the inbox is given; internal/notify has a Wait for tests that returns when no command runs

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A text becomes an item, and a decision about it is answered across a restart

1. **person** runs `nightshift item new demo --text "Add a greeting endpoint"`
2. **nightshift** sends `POST /api/v1/items` and prints the item's number and its thread's URL path
3. **nightshiftd** stores the item in `new` with its thread and appends `item.created`
4. **nightshiftd** opens a decision of a declared kind on the item's thread, as a later package does, writes the entry and runs the notification command with `decision_opened`
5. **person** stops `nightshiftd` with SIGTERM and starts it again
6. **person** runs `nightshift inbox --action`, reads the decision, and runs `nightshift decide <id> --option approve`
7. **nightshiftd** stores the answer and calls the handler registered for the option, which moves the item to `ready`
8. **person** runs `nightshift thread show <id>` and `nightshift item show <N>` and reads the creation, the decision, its answer and the state `ready`

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd run function with its store on disk, the event log and the HTTP API, internal/item, internal/inbox and internal/notify as daemon.Run wires them, the nightshift client's run function, a real notification command (a shell script)

**Setup:**

- a fake Parley hub (internal/hubtest) and a workspace `demo` registered through the end-to-end helper of package 02, which gives the fake hub a workspace with a repository
- `[notify].command` set to a script the test writes that appends its standard input to a file
- a decision kind `test` with the options `approve` and `abandon`, and a handler for `approve` that calls the item service's Transition to `ready`, registered through the same RegisterKind and OnAnswer calls a later package uses, by a hook of the end-to-end helper that runs at each start

**End state:**

- `nightshift item new` exits 0 and prints `item 1` and `thread /api/v1/threads/<id>`
- the script's file holds one JSON document with `event: decision_opened`, `item: 1` and the option keys
- after the restart `nightshift inbox --action` lists the decision
- within 5 seconds of `nightshift decide` exiting 0, `nightshift item show 1` prints `state: ready` and `waiting on: nothing`
- `nightshift thread show` lists entries of the kinds `created`, `decision_opened`, `decision_answered` and `state`, in that order
- a client of `GET /api/v1/events` that connected before the answer received `decision.answered` and `item.updated`

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/daemon/e2e_test.go, extending the helper package 01 wrote: d = startDaemon(cfg, register test kind); code, out = cli(['item','new','demo','--text','Add a greeting endpoint']); assert out == 'item 1\nthread ' + path + '\n'; dec = d.inbox.Open(kind 'test', thread, 'Approve?', recommended 'approve'); eventually the notify file parses with event 'decision_opened'; d.signal(SIGTERM); d = startDaemon(cfg, register test kind); assert cli(['inbox','--action']) contains '1 test demo item 1 Approve?'; s = stream(d); assert cli(['decide','1','--option','approve']).code == 0; eventually cli(['item','show','1']) contains 'state: ready'; assert the kinds of cli(['thread','show',id]) lines; assert s received decision.answered and item.updated
```

### PATH-2: An issue is imported, abandoned, and its workspace removed

1. **person** runs `nightshift item import demo --issue 7`
2. **nightshiftd** requests the issue and the further pages of its comments from the hub with the worker token
3. **hub** answers the issue with the label `bug` and its comments
4. **nightshiftd** stores a `defect` item in `new` with the issue as its source
5. **person** runs the import again and `nightshift workspace remove demo`, and is refused both times with the item named
6. **person** runs `nightshift item abandon <N>`
7. **nightshiftd** calls the abandon hooks, sets the item `abandoned` and marks its thread unread
8. **person** reads the thread in `nightshift inbox --unread` and runs `nightshift workspace remove demo`
9. **nightshiftd** removes the workspace with its item and its threads

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd run function with internal/item, internal/inbox and package 02's internal/workspace as daemon.Run wires them, the hub client of internal/hub against the fake hub's issue routes, the nightshift client's run function, package 02's `workspace remove` and `workspace list` commands among its commands

**Setup:**

- a fake Parley hub (internal/hubtest) holding issue 7 of workspace `demo` with the labels `bug` and `ui` and 150 comments
- the workspace `demo` registered through the end-to-end helper of package 02
- one abandon hook registered by the end-to-end helper that records its call

**End state:**

- the import exits 0; `nightshift item show 1` prints `item 1 (defect)` and `source: issue #7`; `GET /api/v1/items/1` holds 150 comments
- `nightshift workspace list` prints `1 open (1 new)` for demo
- the second import exits 1 with `issue #7 is already item 1`
- the first `workspace remove` exits 1 with `workspace demo has open work items: 1 (new)`
- after the abandon the hook was called once and `nightshift inbox --unread` lists the item's thread
- the second `workspace remove` exits 0; `nightshift item show 1` exits 1; `GET /api/v1/threads` lists no thread of demo

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/daemon/e2e_test.go: d = startDaemon(cfg); assert cli(['item','import','demo','--issue','7']).out starts 'item 1\n'; assert cli(['item','show','1']) contains 'item 1 (defect)'; assert cli(['workspace','list']) contains '1 open (1 new)'; r = cli(['item','import','demo','--issue','7']); assert r.code == 1 and r.err == 'issue #7 is already item 1\n'; r = cli(['workspace','remove','demo']); assert r.code == 1 and r.err == 'workspace demo has open work items: 1 (new)\n'; assert cli(['item','abandon','1']).out == 'item 1 abandoned\n'; assert the hook ran once; assert cli(['inbox','--unread']) names the thread; assert cli(['workspace','remove','demo']).code == 0; assert cli(['item','show','1']).code == 1
```

### PATH-3: The hub is away for 15 minutes, twice

1. **hub** stops answering
2. **nightshiftd** marks the hub unreachable and, once the outage has lasted the threshold, writes `hub unreachable since <time>` to the thread of workspace `demo` and runs the notification command with `hub_unreachable`
3. **person** runs `nightshift inbox --unread` and `nightshift thread show <id>` and reads the entry
4. **hub** answers again, and later stops answering again
5. **nightshiftd** marks the hub reachable, then unreachable, and after the threshold writes the entry and runs the command a second time

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd run function with the hub client and its monitor, the hub watch, internal/inbox and internal/notify as daemon.Run wires them, the nightshift client's run function, a real notification command (a shell script)

**Setup:**

- a fake Parley hub that can be stopped and started on the same address, and the workspace `demo` registered through the end-to-end helper of package 02
- the monitor's probe interval and the hub watch's check interval set to 20 milliseconds and the outage threshold to 200 milliseconds
- `[notify].command` set to a script that appends its standard input to a file

**End state:**

- while the fake hub is down, after the threshold, `nightshift inbox --unread` lists the thread `workspace demo` and `nightshift thread show` prints one `hub_outage` entry
- three thresholds later there is still one such entry and one `hub_unreachable` document in the script's file
- after the fake hub was started, reached and stopped again, a second entry and a second document appear
- the daemon process was the same throughout

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/daemon/e2e_test.go, beside the outage flow of package 01: d = startDaemon(cfg, probe 20ms, check 20ms, threshold 200ms); fakeHub.Stop(); d.hub.Do(any request) fails; eventually cli(['inbox','--unread']) contains 'workspace demo'; assert cli(['thread','show',id]) has 1 line with 'hub_outage hub unreachable since '; sleep 3 thresholds; assert still 1 line and 1 document with event 'hub_unreachable'; fakeHub.Start(); eventually cli(['status']) contains 'reachable'; fakeHub.Stop(); d.hub.Do fails; eventually 2 hub_outage lines and 2 documents
```

# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `go vet ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/inbox/... ./internal/item/... ./internal/notify/... ./internal/cli/... ./internal/daemon/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `01` — uses the API server's Handle, the client's Register and client function, the store's migrations, the event log's Append, the hub client with Available, the monitor's Since() and credential errors, the shutdown steps, the configuration struct, internal/hubtest and the end-to-end helper
- `02` — uses workspace.Service (Get, List, AddRemoveGuard, OnRemoved, Decorate), AddWorkspaceListColumn of internal/cli, the hub client's Workspace, gitclone.Sync, the fake hub's workspaces and git endpoint, and the workspace helper of the end-to-end tests

### 1. Keep threads with entries and unread marks, and serve them (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3.1, REQ-3.2, REQ-3.3, REQ-3.4, REQ-3.5, REQ-3.6

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the thread behaviours to internal/inbox/thread_test.go and the thread route behaviours to internal/inbox/routes_test.go and confirm they fail; keep the fixtures (an inbox over a copy of the store template of internal/store, an injected clock, seeding of threads) in internal/inbox/helpers_test.go, the one helpers file of the package
- 1.2 Add internal/inbox with a store migration registered with internal/store: threads (an id from a counter that is never given twice, the kind item, workspace or brief, the workspace, the item, the title, the unread mark with the seq of the first unread entry, last_activity) and entries (thread, seq, time, kind, text), with uniqueness of the item thread per item, the workspace thread per slug and the one brief thread
- 1.3 Construct the inbox with inbox.New over the store, the event log, a clock and a workspace source (the Get and List of package 02's workspace.Service, an interface here); keep no package-level state, so that tests run in parallel
- 1.4 Add CreateItemThread, which runs inside the transaction of its caller (the item service of task 3), and WorkspaceThread and BriefThread, which return the existing thread or create it, relying on the uniqueness so that concurrent first calls agree
- 1.5 Add Append: refuse an unknown thread, a kind outside ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ and an empty text; otherwise write the entry with the thread's next seq and the clock's time, last_activity and the unread mark in one transaction and append the event thread.updated
- 1.6 Add MarkRead, which appends thread.updated only when the thread was unread, and the reads Thread, Entries and Threads (view, workspace, cursor, page size 50 as a parameter); the cursor is an opaque string holding the last_activity and the id of the last thread of the page
- 1.7 Register GET /api/v1/threads, GET /api/v1/threads/{id} and POST /api/v1/threads/{id}/read through the API server's Handle, answering errors through its helper; the GET of one thread reads it, answers, and then marks it read; `open_decisions` and `decisions` are empty lists and the view `action` is empty until task 2 fills them
- 1.8 Create the inbox in daemon.Run after the store is opened, with package 02's workspace.Service as the workspace source, register its routes, and hand it to the end-to-end helper of internal/daemon/e2e_test.go
- 1.9 Describe the three thread routes, the thread and entry objects, the views, the paging and what marks a thread read in docs/api.md, and add internal/inbox with Append, WorkspaceThread and BriefThread as what later packages call to docs/architecture.md

### 2. Open, answer, close and remind of decisions through a registry of kinds (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4, REQ-5.1

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the decision behaviours to internal/inbox/decision_test.go, the reminder behaviours to internal/inbox/reminder_test.go and the decision route behaviours to internal/inbox/routes_test.go and confirm they fail
- 2.2 Add the store migration for decisions: an id from a counter that is never given twice, the kind, the state open, answered or closed, the thread, the question, the evidence and the options as JSON, what it blocks, the opening time, the answer (option, comment, record, time), whether the answer was carried out, whether its failure was noted, the time of the next attempt, the closing reason and the time of the last reminder
- 2.3 Add the registry on the inbox: RegisterKind, AddOption, OnAnswer(kind, option, handler) and Kind(name), behind a lock and with the refusals of a duplicate or an unknown name; packages register while daemon.Run wires them, before the API serves
- 2.4 Add Open: check the kind, the thread, the question and the recommended key, then store the decision with a copy of the kind's options, append the entry decision_opened with the unread mark and the event decision.opened, in one transaction
- 2.5 Add Answer(ctx, id, Answer{Option, Comment, Record}) with the checks in this order: the decision exists, it is not answered (the error carries the first answer), it is not closed, the option is one of its own, a required comment is not blank; store the answer with an update that applies only to an open decision, so that of concurrent answers one wins and the others get the already-answered error; append the entry and the event in the same transaction
- 2.6 Add the dispatch pass: for every answered decision not carried out whose next attempt is due, call the handler of its kind and option outside any transaction; mark it carried out on nil or when no handler is registered; on an error write the entry decision_effect_failed once and set the next attempt to the clock's time plus the retry interval (a parameter, default 30 seconds)
- 2.7 Run the pass at the start of the daemon, after every stored answer (without the answering request waiting for it) and at the retry interval, from one goroutine that a named shutdown step stops; expose Pending for tests
- 2.8 Add Close with its refusals, its entry and its event, and OpenDecisions(item) for the item service of task 3
- 2.9 Add RemindDue: for every open decision whose opening or last reminder is at least the reminder period (a parameter, default 24 hours) in the past, write one decision_reminder entry with the unread mark and record the time; run it at the start and once a minute from the same goroutine
- 2.10 Register GET /api/v1/decisions, GET /api/v1/decisions/{id} and POST /api/v1/decisions/{id}/answer through Handle, mapping the answer's errors to unknown_option, comment_required, already_answered (with the member `answer`), conflict and not_found; fill `open_decisions` of a thread, `decisions` of one thread and the view `action`
- 2.11 Describe the decision routes, the decision object and the error types in docs/api.md, and the registry (RegisterKind, AddOption, OnAnswer, Open, Close) with the rule that a handler may be called twice in docs/architecture.md
